conviction_note: Findings net to about zero: a consensus beat is likely, because Disney beat adj EPS in all three FY26 quarters, and cost cuts, the buyback and an easy Q1 sports comp lean up. Against that, the stock has run about 17% since the August print to within 0.8% of its 52-week high, 25-delta put skew is +9.4 vol points, and a reaffirm-only FY27 'double-digit' guide sits below a street FY27 of $7.43-7.50. p_up 48 on abs 6.8 gives -0.27; the two measurements agree that there is no edge.
bar: Q4 FY26 adj EPS consensus $1.67 on revenue ~$25.26B with a whisper of $1.74 (Earnings Whispers, 2026-11-10, https://www.earningswhispers.com/article/DIS/23094). Second estimate: $1.69 on $25.19B (TIKR, 2026-11-03, https://www.tikr.com/blog/disney-dis-stock-up-month-take-profits-or-buy-more). Company guide: Q4 total segment OI ~$4.9B including the 53rd week, and FY26 adj EPS growth ~16% including it (~$6.88 on FY25 $5.93) (Q3 call, https://s206.q4cdn.com/979796730/files/doc_events/2026/Aug/05/q3-fy26-earnings-transcript.pdf). With Q1 $1.63, Q2 $1.57 and Q3 $2.06, that guide implies Q4 of about $1.62, so consensus sits slightly above the guide. The two estimate sources agree within $0.02, so the bar is sourced. FY27 bar: street $7.43 (EW) to $7.50 (TIKR) against the company's 'double-digit growth excluding the 53rd week' off ~$6.64, a floor of about $7.30.
positioning_check: Short interest is low and not crowded. FINRA 2026-08-14 settlement: ~18.9M shares, 1.7 days to cover (https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/dis/short-interest/). 2026-09-30 settlement: ~19.6M shares, 1.1% of float, 2.7 days to cover, trend falling (https://equibles.com/stocks/dis/shortinterest). ORTEX on 2026-11-03: ~1.3% of free float, 2.8 days to cover, borrow cost 0.38% (https://app.ortex.com/s/NYSE/DIS). There is no squeeze mechanism to shrink a negative. Options (baseline): 25-delta skew +9.43 vol points (downside paid), put/call OI 0.72, event-implied move 5.96% (straddle 6.26%), against a median of 7.4% over the last 7 prints. Run-up: 20 days +8.3%, 5 days -0.36%, 0.8% below the 52-week high.

expectations.price_path: Baseline: 5-day -0.36%, 20-day +8.3%, 0.8% below the 52-week high and 28.4% above the 52-week low. No sector ETF series was found for the same days. Against the market: +9.5% from 2026-10-01 to 10-30 vs S&P 500 -1.1% (Trefis, https://www.trefis.com/stock/dis/articles/621802/which-dates-could-move-disney-stock-most/2026-11-02), and +~17% since the 2026-08-05 report vs S&P -3%, ~$15 above the ~$104 200-day average (Earnings Whispers 2026-11-10, https://www.earningswhispers.com/article/DIS/23094).
expectations.vs_targets: Spot $118.69 against a mean target of ~$127 (TIKR, 2026-11-03, https://www.tikr.com/blog/disney-dis-stock-up-month-take-profits-or-buy-more). Citi raised to $140 from $135 on 2026-10-16 (same source). An undated aggregator snippet gives a street-high of $163, which is unverified. Spot is ~7% below the mean target.
expectations.whisper_or_buyside_bar: Earnings Whisper $1.74 vs $1.67 consensus (https://www.earningswhispers.com/article/DIS/23094, 2026-11-10). TIKR (2026-11-03): the street needs management to 'reaffirm its double-digit outlook for fiscal 2027', and if it is trimmed the rally 'has nothing behind it but a higher multiple'. EW: analysts still discount the FY27 plan, at $7.43 vs what it calls management's ~$7.91.
expectations.last_print: Q3 FY26 (2026-08-05): adj EPS $2.06 vs $1.86-1.88 expected, revenue $25.2B vs $25.39-25.41B (a slight miss), segment OI +21% ahead of guide, FY26/FY27 reaffirmed, buyback raised to >= $9B (https://www.newsquawk.com/headlines/disney-dis-q3-2026-usd-adj-eps-206-exp-186-revenue-252bln-exp-2539bln). Stock +3.65% on the day (baseline).
expectations.short_interest_trend: 2026-08-14: ~18.9M shares, 1.7 DTC (https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/dis/short-interest/). 2026-09-30: ~19.6M, 1.1% float, 2.7 DTC, 'falling' (https://equibles.com/stocks/dis/shortinterest). ORTEX 2026-11-03: ~1.3% FF, 2.8 DTC (https://app.ortex.com/s/NYSE/DIS). Low and flat.
expectations.real_bar: To rise from 0.8% off its high after a ~17% run since August, Disney probably needs adj EPS near the $1.74 whisper with segment OI >= $4.9B, plus an FY27 outlook quantified at or above the street's ~$7.43-7.50 (low-teens growth off the $6.64 ex-53rd-week base), backed by a cost-savings number and an FY27 buyback >= $9B. A bare 'double-digit' reaffirm probably does not clear it.

next_guide.street_next_quarter: not found (no Q1 FY27 EPS consensus located)
next_guide.company_current_guide: FY27: double-digit adj EPS growth excluding the 53rd week, reaffirmed on 2026-08-05 (https://s206.q4cdn.com/979796730/files/doc_events/2026/Aug/05/q3-fy26-earnings-transcript.pdf) and repeated by the CFO on 2026-09-09 (https://s206.q4cdn.com/979796730/files/doc_events/2026/Sep/09/hj-gs-2026-0909.pdf). Off ~$6.64 ex-53rd week, that implies >= ~$7.30.
next_guide.basis: The CFO repeated 'double-digit' on 2026-09-09 with no quantification and steered SVOD toward OI dollars and more content spend. That points to a maintained guide, possibly with detail. The cost program reported by Bloomberg on 2026-11-02 (some units targeting 20% savings) is the main route to a raise, but the CFO says savings are redeployed into growth.

findings.finding: The stock goes into the print at its high with expectations raised. It is +~17% since the 2026-08-05 report vs S&P -3%, +9.5% in October vs S&P -1.1%, +8.3% over 20 days, and 0.8% below its 52-week high. The whisper is $1.74 vs $1.67 consensus. On this name 2 of the last 4 beats were sold (Feb 2026 -7.4% on an EPS beat, Nov 2025 -7.75%).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 FY26 (2026-02-02): adj EPS $1.63 vs $1.57, stock -7.4% (https://finviz.com/news/296138/why-disney-dis-shares-are-getting-obliterated-today). Q4 FY25 (2025-11-13): -7.75% as Entertainment lagged and revenue missed (https://seekingalpha.com/news/4521276-disney-falls-after-its-entertainment-segment-lags-in-fq4). Beats bought after a sell-down: Q2 FY26 +7.54%, Q3 FY26 +3.65%.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the run-up IS the market's expectation. The point is that the beat-and-reaffirm that bought +3.65% to +7.54% from a lower base now has to clear a higher real bar. If the market had already de-risked this, the stock would sit off its high rather than 0.8% below it.
findings.independence: Trefis, 2026-11-02 (https://www.trefis.com/stock/dis/articles/621802/which-dates-could-move-disney-stock-most/2026-11-02): +9.5% in October vs S&P -1.1%. Baseline run_up_20d +8.3% and pct_from_52w_high -0.8%.

findings.finding: Disney beat adj EPS in every FY26 quarter: Q1 $1.63 vs $1.57, Q2 $1.57 vs ~$1.50, Q3 $2.06 vs $1.86-1.88. Q4 consensus of $1.67-1.69 sits only ~$0.05-0.07 above the ~$1.62 implied by the FY guide ($6.88 - 1.63 - 1.57 - 2.06), so a beat is the base case. Revenue missed in Q3 ($25.2B vs $25.39-25.41B) and in Q4 FY25.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: EPS beats got -7.4% (Feb 2026), +7.54% (May 2026) and +3.65% (Aug 2026). The reaction tracked the guide, not the size of the beat.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: three straight beats and a whisper above consensus mean a beat is expected. Only a beat well above $1.74 would be new.
findings.independence: Q2 beat $1.57 vs ~$1.50 (https://www.tikr.com/blog/disney-stock-jumps-7-after-q2-revenue-and-eps-both-beat-expectations). Q1 beat (https://finviz.com/news/296138/why-disney-dis-shares-are-getting-obliterated-today). FY guide in the Q3 transcript (https://s206.q4cdn.com/979796730/files/doc_events/2026/Aug/05/q3-fy26-earnings-transcript.pdf).

findings.finding: The FY27 street ($7.43 EW, $7.50 TIKR) sits above the floor of the company's only FY27 guide. 'Double-digit adj EPS growth excluding the 53rd week' off ~$6.64 is >= ~$7.30, while the street implies ~12-13% growth. Measured against the reported FY26 $6.88, which includes the extra week, the street is only +8-9%. A reaffirm of 'double-digit' without a number reads at or below the street.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: November prints carry the next-year guide. Nov 2025 -7.75% on revenue miss and guide tone. May 2026 +7.54% when FY27 double-digit was first set and the buyback raised (https://www.rttnews.com/3648058/disney-q2-profit-down-sees-earnings-growth-in-fy26-fy27-plans-at-least-8-bln-buyback-stock-up.aspx). Feb 2026 -7.4% on a 'just okay' guide.
findings.why_not_priced: Previews quote '$7.91' as management's FY27 number (EW), a figure that is not in the company transcript. That suggests part of the market reads the plan as more aggressive than the company's 'double-digit' wording. If the gap were priced, previews would anchor on ~$7.30.
findings.independence: CFO on 2026-09-09 repeated 'double-digit underlying growth in fiscal '27' without a number (https://s206.q4cdn.com/979796730/files/doc_events/2026/Sep/09/hj-gs-2026-0909.pdf). Same company, different document. Street figures: https://www.tikr.com/blog/disney-dis-stock-up-month-take-profits-or-buy-more.

findings.finding: A cost program sized after the last call could underpin the FY27 guide. Bloomberg (via Cord Cutters, 2026-11-02) reports Disney is preparing 'thousands' of job cuts, with some managers told to find 20% annual savings and parks, TV networks and studio carrying more. It follows a third layoff round on 2026-09-29, and on the Q3 call the CFO flagged 'meaningful reductions to cost, including labor and SG&A' with an update to come. Disney had ~231,000 employees.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The 2023 restructuring ($5.5B savings, ~7,000 jobs) was announced with Q1 FY23 results in Feb 2023 and the stock rose after hours. Its stock-level reaction is not in the baseline.
findings.why_not_priced: The scale is unquantified ('planning stage'), so no savings number is in the street's FY27 $7.43-7.50. A dollar savings target on the call would be new. The caveat is built into the size: the CFO says savings will be redeployed into content, parks and tech, which caps how much reaches EPS.
findings.independence: Q3 call (https://s206.q4cdn.com/979796730/files/doc_events/2026/Aug/05/q3-fy26-earnings-transcript.pdf, CFO on cost reductions). 2026-09-29 layoff round (https://www.roic.ai/news/disney-cuts-hundreds-more-jobs-in-third-layoff-wave-of-2026-09-29-2026). The CFO on 2026-09-09 described a 'virtuous circle of reducing costs, reinvestment' (https://s206.q4cdn.com/979796730/files/doc_events/2026/Sep/09/hj-gs-2026-0909.pdf).

findings.finding: On 2026-09-09 the CFO said SVOD will now prioritise 'absolute OI dollar growth rather than just margins'. He also said Disney 'need[s] to invest more in content', with international content to go up 'by a lot on a percentage basis', and that margins will not go 'below double-digits'. That signals an FY27 DTC margin at or near FY26's ~double-digit level rather than expansion. Q3 SVOD margin was 13%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Streaming OI was the swing line in Feb 2026 (Q1 streaming OI +72%, stock -7.4% on overall guide/CEO news). There is no clean instance of a DTC-margin guide moving the stock.
findings.why_not_priced: The CFO said it at a conference rather than in guidance, and previews still frame SVOD around the 13% margin and the double-digit target being 'within reach' (EW 2026-11-10). If it were priced, previews would model flat DTC margins for FY27. The CFO also said the spend 'won't be disruptive to the overall algorithm', which keeps this small.
findings.independence: Same document as the cost-program and Avengers presales findings, which share the 2026-09-09 transcript (opposite or unrelated directions, both can be true). Q3 call: 'continued ... competitive in streaming ... pricing pressure' (https://s206.q4cdn.com/979796730/files/doc_events/2026/Aug/05/q3-fy26-earnings-transcript.pdf).

findings.finding: The CFO said on 2026-09-09 that Avengers: Doomsday (December 2026, fiscal Q1 FY27) had '$50 million of presales' three months out. That supports the Q1 FY27 Entertainment outlook against a Q1 FY26 that had Zootopia 2 (~$1.4B worldwide) and Avatar: Fire and Ash, and in which Entertainment OI still fell 35% to $1.1B on marketing costs.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 Entertainment guide commentary weighed in Nov 2025 (-7.75%) and Feb 2026 (-7.4%).
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the slate is public. The Q1 FY27 Entertainment comp is what management will guide to, and the Q1 FY26 base was weak (-35%) despite big films. If the market expected an easy Q1, previews would mention it. None found did.
findings.independence: Q1 FY26 Entertainment OI -35% to $1.1B (https://finviz.com/news/296138/why-disney-dis-shares-are-getting-obliterated-today). Zootopia 2 grosses (https://tribune.com.pk/story/2583476/avatar-fire-and-ash-opens-to-345m-worldwide-as-zootopia-2-reaches-127bn-global-total).

findings.finding: Comcast (2026-10-22): Universal theme parks revenue -4.4%, adj EBITDA -17%. It cited 'near-term demand pressure in Orlando' from macro and geopolitical headwinds and 'competitors adjusting marketing faster', said Q4 2026 and 1H27 would look similar, and expects a return to growth only in 2H27.
findings.link: Same destination market (Orlando) for the same quarter (Jul-Sep). Walt Disney World is the largest part of Disney's domestic parks, and Experiences was 'about 85% of earnings' together with Entertainment, per the CFO on 2026-09-09. Part of Universal's decline is lapping Epic Universe's May 2025 opening, which is specific to Comcast. 'Competitors adjusting marketing faster' points to Disney promotions, a share gain with a per-cap risk.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Domestic parks were the swing line in Q3 FY26: attendance +3% and per-cap +4% helped the +3.65% reaction. Q2 FY26 domestic attendance was -1%.
findings.why_not_priced: Comcast spoke after Disney last did (2026-08-05/09-09). Net of the rest: Disney's own Q3 showed WDW growing while Universal fell, and Experiences is guided to the high end of high-single-digit for FY26, so the Q4 effect is small. The FY27 Orlando comment (softness into 1H27) is what Disney's FY27 Experiences guide must answer.
findings.independence: Advan foot traffic (https://advanresearch.com/insights/the-end-of-the-2026-theme-park-season-disney-won-florida-and-universal-won-california-seaworld-is-waiting-for-next-year) points the other way for Disney in the summer, consistent with share shift rather than a market-wide decline.

findings.finding: Advan observed domestic foot traffic, Memorial Day to Labor Day 2026: Magic Kingdom 'led in observed visits growth for both the season and the July & August period', and Disney's other three Orlando parks 'also performed strongly', with visit duration up year on year. Disneyland visits were 'modestly lower YoY'. International visitors are excluded and no percentages are given.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Domestic attendance +3% in Q3 FY26 helped +3.65%. -1% in Q2 FY26 was sold until the print beat.
findings.why_not_priced: The data is proprietary and few previews carry it. It lands inside the company's guide, though: Experiences is already at the high end of high-single-digit for FY26, and WDW bookings were 'up nicely' on 2026-08-05. So it mostly confirms the guided quarter.
findings.independence: Q3 call: WDW forward bookings 'up nicely', cruise bookings 'very healthy', and Asia (Shanghai, Hong Kong) weakness continuing into Q4 (https://s206.q4cdn.com/979796730/files/doc_events/2026/Aug/05/q3-fy26-earnings-transcript.pdf).

findings.finding: Cruise peers reported strong results after Disney last spoke. Royal Caribbean Q3 2026 (late October): revenue +9%, FY guide raised to $17.85-17.95, booking volumes up mid-teens since July, 2027 sailings up high-teens. Carnival Q3 (2026-09-29): record 2027 booked occupancy and pricing, customer deposits a record ~$7.6B.
findings.link: Same product (cruise) and same quarter. Disney Cruise Line sits in Experiences and added ~50% guest rooms over two years (CFO 2026-09-09). DCL's share of Experiences OI is not disclosed.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Cruise capacity was cited as a driver of Q3 guest growth +4%. It has no separate reaction history.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. Disney already called its cruise bookings 'very healthy' and said it 'can't fill all the demand' (2026-09-09). This supports an FY27 Experiences guide but is a small share of the company.
findings.independence: Carnival record 2027 bookings (https://gcaptain.com/carnival-posts-record-1-9-billion-profit-as-2027-bookings-hit-new-high/). Disney CFO 2026-09-09 transcript.

findings.finding: Netflix (2026-10-20) cut its 2026 ad revenue forecast to ~$2.7B from ~$3B, citing delayed ad-product rollouts and partner integrations. Q3 revenue growth was 12%, its slowest in three years. Disney's CFO had said SVOD ad pricing 'softness' would 'continue in Q4' because of new supply.
findings.link: Same product (US SVOD advertising) and the same buyers. Netflix attributes its cut to its own ad tech; Disney attributes its softness to supply.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: SVOD ad growth slowed in Q3 FY26 without hurting the +3.65% reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: Disney pre-warned of Q4 SVOD ad softness, so this lands inside guidance. Netflix's cause is partly company-specific.
findings.independence: Disney CFO 2026-09-09 (https://s206.q4cdn.com/979796730/files/doc_events/2026/Sep/09/hj-gs-2026-0909.pdf). Netflix ad forecast cut (https://www.marketingdive.com/news/netflix-lowers-ad-revenue-forecast-by-10-continues-to-beef-up-ad-suite/833571/).

findings.finding: Fox fiscal Q1 FY27 (Jul-Sep 2026, reported 2026-11-02): ad revenue +47% company-wide and TV segment ad +60%, driven by the FIFA World Cup, midterm political and Tubi. Disney's CFO had called political and healthcare categories strong and live sports ads 'on fire'.
findings.link: Same quarter and the same national and local TV ad market: ABC owned stations (political), ESPN and ABC sports ad sales. Fox's +47% is inflated by World Cup rights Disney does not hold, so only the political and sports-ad tone transfers.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Sports advertising +10% in Q1 FY26 was more than offset by costs. No separate reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: Fox reported after Disney's last statement. Midterm political spend landing in Disney's FQ4 and FQ1 linear and stations is a proxy, not confirmed by Disney, and is small relative to the company.
findings.independence: Disney CFO 2026-09-09 transcript on political and healthcare strength (https://s206.q4cdn.com/979796730/files/doc_events/2026/Sep/09/hj-gs-2026-0909.pdf).

findings.finding: Charter Q3 2026 (pro forma with Cox): video customers -77k vs -121k a year earlier, legacy Charter -38k. Coverage attributes the slower loss to bundling streaming apps into Spectrum video. Video customers -1.8% over the last twelve months.
findings.link: Charter is one of Disney's largest MVPD distributors (share of Disney affiliate fees not disclosed). Its sub count drives ESPN and linear affiliate revenue, and the Spectrum bundle includes Disney+ and ESPN apps.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Lower affiliate fees offset Sports ad growth in Q1 FY26 (Sports OI -23%). No direct reaction history.
findings.why_not_priced: A counterparty number dated after Disney last spoke. The slower cord-cutting eases the Sports and linear affiliate drag at the margin. It is small and one distributor.
findings.independence: Cord Cutters News on Spectrum Q3 losses (https://cordcuttersnews.com/?p=259509).

findings.finding: Q1 FY27 Sports has an easy comp. Q1 FY26 Sports OI was $191M, down 23%, and included ~$110M of lost operating income from the YouTube TV carriage suspension. That should make the Q1 FY27 Sports guide read better year on year.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q1 FY26 print with the YouTube TV hit fell 7.4% (2026-02-02), mostly on other items.
findings.why_not_priced: It is public history, so it is largely in models. It matters only if Disney's Q1 commentary frames Sports as growing. Small.
findings.independence: IBC: the blackout cost $110M (https://www.ibc.org/distribution-consumption/news/disney-s-youtube-tv-blackout-cost-110m/22993).

findings.finding: FY26 buybacks were raised to at least $9B (from ~$7B originally, then $8B), funded partly by cash set aside for the OpenAI deal and the ~$1.2B sale of Disney's 50% A+E stake to Hearst. The CFO said Disney is 'not really looking to build cash'. The FY27 buyback number should come with this release.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Buyback raises came with the +7.54% (May 2026, to >= $8B) and +3.65% (Aug 2026, to >= $9B) reactions.
findings.why_not_priced: No FY27 buyback figure is in the previews found. EW still quotes the stale $8B. A >= $9-10B FY27 plan would be in line; less would disappoint. The direction is uncertain, so the size is small.
findings.independence: A+E sale ~$1.2B (https://www.thewrap.com/industry-news/deals-ma/disney-to-sell-a-and-e-media-stake-to-hearst/).

findings.finding: Disney raised streaming prices from 2026-09-23 for new subscribers and on billing cycles from 2026-10-21 for existing ones. Disney+ Premium (no ads) went from $18.99 to $21.49 (+13%), and the Disney+/Hulu ad-free bundle from $19.99 to $21.99. The ad-supported bundle and ESPN Unlimited bundles were unchanged.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Prior October price rises (2024, 2025) carried no separate reaction. Churn risk is discussed on calls.
findings.why_not_priced: It is public and a recurring annual move, so it is mostly in FY27 DTC models. It lands inside the double-digit plan.
findings.independence: Disney Food Blog, 2026-09-23 (https://www.disneyfoodblog.com/2026/09/23/your-disney-subscription-probably-just-got-more-expensive/).

findings.finding: Options lean to the downside into the print: 25-delta skew +9.43 vol points (puts over calls), put/call OI 0.72, event-implied move 5.96% vs a 7.4% median of the last 7 realised moves. Short interest is low (~1.1-1.3% of float, 2.7-2.8 days to cover), so there is no squeeze fuel against a negative outcome.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 4 of the last 7 prints were down (baseline). The median absolute move of 7.4% exceeds the implied 5.96%.
findings.why_not_priced: The skew is the market's own statement, so this is priced by definition. It is filed because a long thesis would need to say why the skew is wrong, and nothing found does.
findings.independence: ORTEX 2026-11-03 (https://app.ortex.com/s/NYSE/DIS). Baseline options block (skew 9.43).

findings.finding: Insider: EVP Controller Brent Woodford exercised 3,618 options ($105.21, expiring 2026-12-21) and sold them at $117.00 on 2026-11-04 under a 10b5-1 plan adopted 2026-02-24. That is routine. Disney has filed no 8-K since 2026-08-05: no reaffirmation and no pre-release.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: none
findings.why_not_priced: Not information. A pre-scheduled plan sale of expiring options. Filed for completeness.
findings.independence: EDGAR submissions list (https://data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK0001744489.json): only one 8-K (Item 2.02, 2026-08-05) since August.

findings.finding: Disney placed a $20M stalking-horse bid for Character.AI assets. It is not final, and on 2026-10-23, 31 states plus DC objected to the proposed sale rules.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: none
findings.why_not_priced: Immaterial at $20M with no path to the guide.
findings.independence: none

findings.finding: Fiscal Q4 studio slate was mixed. Live-action Moana (opened July 2026) underperformed at about $281.5M worldwide, the second-lowest live-action remake, while Toy Story 5 crossed $1B. Management had already called Moana and Mandalorian below box-office expectations on 2026-08-05 and kept the Q4 guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Entertainment lagging drove the Nov 2025 drop (-7.75%) (https://seekingalpha.com/news/4521276-disney-falls-after-its-entertainment-segment-lags-in-fq4).
findings.why_not_priced: Known and inside guidance. Only a write-down would be new, and none is signalled.
findings.independence: Q3 call on Moana and Mandalorian (https://s206.q4cdn.com/979796730/files/doc_events/2026/Aug/05/q3-fy26-earnings-transcript.pdf). Moana opening (https://lasvegassun.com/news/2026/jul/12/disneys-live-action-moana-crashes-to-shore-with-an/).

findings.finding: Tariff refunds: ~$100M of refunds lifted Q3 Experiences segment OI. The CFO said there would be 'a smaller benefit, if one at all, in Q4' and the full-year impact would be 'basically nothing'.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: none
findings.why_not_priced: Immaterial and pre-announced. It flattered the Q3 Experiences OI comparison, so a Q4 comparison without it is slightly harder.
findings.independence: none

outside_window.finding: Disney+ ecosystem expansion (games, merchandise, parks booking inside Disney+) starts in spring 2027.
Avengers: Doomsday box office (release December 2026), with $50M presales three months out.
